notes: Plassey 1757 gave the Anglican-Christian EIC control via Mir Jafar. Company kept Christianity but from 1803 managed and funded Puri's Jagannath temple (pilgrim tax, annual payments) until 1840s withdrawal; patronage, not conversion. Bengal Hindu-majority with large Muslim minority.

Kassites had own gods (Shuqamuna, Shumaliya). Agum II returned Marduk's statue to Babylon 24 years after the 1595 sack (dating debated); Kassite kings built Babylonian temples, keeping Kassite gods as royal patrons. Kassite was unwritten; Akkadian cuneiform used.

Both Muslim: Aq Qoyunlu (conventionally Sunni, though Iranica doubts a sharp contrast) defeated by Esma'il's Qizilbash 1501-1503; Safavids were a militant Shi'ite Sufi order who made Twelver Shi'ism Iran's unifying faith. Same tradition.

notes: Hammurabi defeated Rim-Sin of Larsa in 1763 BCE. Both Amorite-led Mesopotamian states shared the Sumero-Akkadian pantheon (sun-god temple at Larsa; Hammurabi's stela shows Shamash) and cuneiform scribal culture.

notes: Assyria expelled the Kushites from Lower Egypt (671-663) but ruled through Egyptian vassals; the Saite Psamtik I took Thebes in 656 and patronized Egyptian temples. Coded the Saite ruling group (Egyptian); Assyrian overlords kept Mesopotamian religion.

notes: Rome annexed Crete 67 BCE (Gortyn capital). Roman state cult was retained; Greek gods were already assimilated before conquest, and Augustus embraced and reshaped Greek cults such as the Eleusinian Mysteries. Patronage alongside Roman cult, not adoption; boundary blurry.

Database Jainism kept (Nandas linked to Jain patronage; population likely mixed). Chandragupta rose with Brahman adviser Kautilya (Brahmanical, inferred); Jain tradition says he accepted Jainism from Bhadrabahu and died at Shravanabelagola c. 297 BCE. Pre-Ashokan writing debated.

Odoacer (476) and Theodoric's Ostrogoths (489-493) were Arian Christians ruling Nicene Catholic Italy; same tradition under the brief's sect rule. Both kept the Roman civil administration; Gothic was also written.
